mainTopic: How we know that grain's year follows its first third of growth, and whether the חכמים can measure exactly one-third
overview: The גמרא proves that grain which reached one-third of its growth during the seventh year keeps its שמיטה rules until סוכות of the eighth year. The proof comes from ״וחג האסיף בצאת השנה״: ״אסיף״ means harvest, and grain harvested on סוכות must have reached a third before ראש השנה. רבי ירמיה asks how the חכמים can tell exactly one-third from slightly less. רבי זירא answers that all the measures of the חכמים have exact cutoffs, like forty סאה, a כביצה, and three-by-three for מדרס. רבי ירמיה then takes back his question, citing the first עומר in ארץ ישראל. That עומר came from grain that had not reached a third while a גוי owned it, so they must have been able to judge the one-third point. The גמרא rejects this proof: because ארץ ישראל is called ״ארץ צבי״, the grain may have had no growth at all and still ripened quickly. Then רבי חנינא shows from another פסוק that ״אסיף״ can mean gathering the waste of the threshing floor, which knocks down the original proof. The גמרא begins a new source, a ברייתא of רבי יונתן בן יוסף on ״לשלש השנים״, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Maybe the rule covers grain that never grew in the seventh year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that the rule is about grain that reached a third. Maybe the Torah means grain that did not grow at all in the seventh year.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the grain did not enter the seventh year at all, and still the Torah says: keep שמיטה rules for it until סוכות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge against the reading it just gave. Who says the פסוק is about grain that reached one-third before ראש השנה? Maybe it is about grain that did not grow at all in the seventh year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the גמרא said the פסוק links שמיטה to סוכות to teach that grain which reached a third in year seven stays under שמיטה rules until סוכות. The challenge says the פסוק itself never mentions 'one-third.' So maybe the Torah extends שמיטה to all grain until סוכות, even grain with no growth in year seven.

keyTerms.meaning: Entered (here: grew during the seventh year)

phrases.english: But perhaps it did not enter at all,
phrases.notes: He means the grain did not grow at all during the seventh year, not even a third, before ראש השנה.

phrases.english: and still the Merciful One says: keep שמיטה rules
and continue until the festival of סוכות!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier reading, from before this section, that the פסוק refers to grain that reached a third.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the סוכות extension applies only to grain that reached one-third before ראש השנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק does not say 'one-third.' It could just as well mean grain that did not grow at all in year seven.

steps.title: Rejecting the challenge with the פסוק about the harvest festival
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the challenge cannot be right. It brings the פסוק ״וחג האסיף בצאת השנה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't think that, for it is written: 'And the festival of gathering, at the end of the year.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by quoting a פסוק. This sets up the next lines, which will explain how the פסוק proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key words are ״בצאת השנה״, 'at the end of the year.' סוכות falls after ראש השנה, yet the Torah links it to the old year. The next steps explain which crop this refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: At the going-out (end) of the year

phrases.english: It should not enter your mind,
as it is written: 'And the festival of gathering, at the end of the year,'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule might apply even to grain that did not grow in year seven.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק will show it applies only to grain that reached a third before ראש השנה.

steps.title: What does 'gathering' mean? Not simply the gathering season
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what ״אסיף״ means. It rejects the simple meaning of 'the festival in gathering season' because the same פסוק already says 'when you gather.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'gathering'? If you say it means the festival that comes at gathering time, the פסוק already says 'when you gather.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the word ״אסיף״. It throws out the obvious meaning because the פסוק would then be repeating itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the same פסוק says ״באספך את מעשיך מן השדה״, 'when you gather your work from the field.' That already tells us סוכות comes at gathering time. So ״אסיף״ must be teaching something new.

keyTerms.meaning: If you will say (offers a suggestion that will be rejected)

phrases.english: What is 'gathering'?
If we say: a festival that comes at gathering time —
but it is already written: 'when you gather.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the פסוק quoted in step 2 by first ruling out the simple meaning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact meaning of the word ״אסיף״ in the פסוק.

steps.title: 'Gathering' means harvest, so the grain reached a third before ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: ״אסיף״ means harvest. Grain harvested on סוכות must have reached a third before ראש השנה, and the Torah still calls that time 'the end of the year.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, 'gathering' means harvesting. The חכמים know that any grain harvested on סוכות surely reached one-third before ראש השנה, and the Torah calls it 'at the end of the year.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real meaning of ״אסיף״, which is harvest. This completes the answer to the challenge in step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain ripe for harvest on סוכות must already have reached a third of its growth before ראש השנה. The Torah calls this harvest 'at the end of the year,' meaning it still belongs to the old year. So the old year's rules, including שמיטה, stay with grain that reached a third before ראש השנה, not with grain that never grew in year seven.
steps.whatToRemember: Grain that reached one-third of its growth before ראש השנה counts as the old year's crop. That is why a seventh-year crop keeps its שמיטה rules into the eighth year until סוכות.

phrases.english: Rather, what is 'gathering'? Harvesting.
And the חכמים have it established
that any grain which is harvested on the festival,
it is known that it reached one-third
before ראש השנה,
and the Torah calls it 'at the end of the year.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct meaning after step 3 ruled out the simple one, and so finishes answering step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״אסיף״ means harvest. Grain harvested on סוכות reached a third before ראש השנה and is counted as the old year's crop.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה asks how the חכמים can tell one-third from less
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא whether the חכמים can really tell exactly one-third of growth apart from a little less.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to רבי זירא: Can the חכמים really tell the difference between one-third and less than one-third?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens about the measure itself. רבי ירמיה doubts that anyone can be so exact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole rule depends on the line between one-third and just under one-third. If no one can see that difference, it seems hard to build a הלכה on it. רבי ירמיה is questioning whether such a fine measure can work.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא known for asking sharp, borderline questions

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: רבי ירמיה said to רבי זירא:
And do the חכמים know precisely
between one-third and less than one-third?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the 'one-third' measure that step 4 relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the חכמים know which grain reached exactly one-third.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Such a fine difference seems impossible to notice, so how can a הלכה depend on it?

steps.title: רבי זירא: All the measures of the חכמים work this way
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא scolds רבי ירמיה for stepping outside the הלכה. All the measures of the חכמים are exact like this.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Didn't I tell you not to take yourself outside the הלכה? All the measures of the חכמים are like this.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers with a firm rebuke. He tells רבי ירמיה that this kind of exact line is normal for every measure of the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every measure of the חכמים, like a כזית or forty סאה, has an exact cutoff where a tiny bit less changes the law. Questioning this one measure would mean questioning all of them. So the 'one-third' rule stands like the others.

keyTerms.meaning: The measures set by the חכמים

steps.whatToRemember: The measures of the חכמים have exact cutoffs, and the הלכה follows them even where the difference is tiny.

phrases.english: He said to him: Didn't I tell you
do not take yourself out
beyond the הלכה?
All the measures of the חכמים are like this.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו אָמֵינָא לָךְ לָא תַּפֵּיק נַפְשָׁךְ לְבַר מֵהִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's question from step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A cutoff as fine as one-third versus slightly less cannot be the basis of a הלכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: All the measures of the חכמים have exact cutoffs, so this one is valid too.

steps.title: Examples of exact measures
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא finishes his answer by listing measures where even a tiny shortfall changes the הלכה: forty סאה for a מקוה, a כביצה for food impurity, and three-by-three טפחים for מדרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person can immerse in forty סאה of water, but if it is missing even a tiny bit, he cannot immerse in it. An egg-sized piece of food makes other food impure, but if it is missing even a sesame seed, it does not. A cloth three by three can become impure through מדרס, but if it is missing even one thread, it cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא is still answering. He gives three examples to show that every measure of the חכמים works this way: exactly at the line it counts, and a hair below it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה wondered whether anyone could really tell 'one third' apart from 'a little less.' רבי זירא answers that this is how all שיעורים work. Even a tiny shortfall, like a קורטוב, a sesame seed, or one thread, changes the הלכה completely.

keyTerms.meaning: Forty סאה, the minimum amount of water for a kosher מקוה
The size of an egg, the amount of food needed to spread טומאה to other food
A sesame seed, a tiny amount
Impurity that comes from a זב or similar person sitting, lying, or treading on an item

steps.whatToRemember: The measures of the חכמים are sharp lines. Exactly at the measure counts, and even a tiny bit less does not.

phrases.english: In forty סאה one immerses,
but in forty סאה missing a קורטוב —
phrases.notes: A קורטוב is a tiny amount of liquid, only a few drops.

phrases.english: he cannot immerse in them.
An egg-bulk makes food impure,
an egg-bulk missing a sesame seed —
does not make food impure.
Three by three can become impure through מדרס,
phrases.notes: He means a piece of cloth three טפחים by three טפחים.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה חָסֵר נִימָא אַחַת —
phrases.english: three by three missing one thread —
cannot become impure through מדרס.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and illustrates רבי זירא's answer from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that this is how all measures work
steps.terutzHavaAmina: You might think a measure like 'one third' is too fine to judge exactly.
steps.terutzMaskana: All שיעורים of the חכמים are exact lines, so 'one third' is no different.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה takes back his question
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה later says that his question was not a real question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Later רבי ירמיה said: What I said is nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה takes back his own challenge from step 5. This also sets up the next move, because he is about to bring a case that shows why his question was wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, רבי ירמיה doubted that the חכמים could really pinpoint one third of growth. Now he admits there is a source showing that they can and do judge exactly when grain reaches a third.

keyTerms.meaning: Afterward he said, a sign that someone is changing his position
It is nothing, meaning it was not a valid point

phrases.english: Then רבי ירמיה said:
What I said is nothing.
phrases.notes: He is talking about his own question from step 5, whether the חכמים can measure an exact third.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: לָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא דַּאֲמַרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Withdraws the challenge that רבי זירא had pushed back on in steps 6–7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי ירמיה's own challenge from step 5
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is a known case where the חכמים clearly judge when grain reaches a third, which he is about to bring.

steps.title: Where did the first עומר in ארץ ישראל come from?
steps.stepSummary: The other scholars asked רב כהנא where the עומר came from when בני ישראל first entered the land. It could not come from grain grown by a גוי, because the Torah says 'your harvest.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The colleagues asked רב כהנא: The עומר that בני ישראל brought when they entered the land, where did they bring it from? If you say it grew while the land was owned by a גוי, the Torah says 'your harvest,' and not the harvest of a גוי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה brings the source behind his retraction: a question the scholars asked רב כהנא. The question sets up a problem. The grain they found in the land had grown under non-Jewish ownership, so how could it be used for the עומר?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עומר must come from 'your harvest,' meaning grain that belongs to Jews. When בני ישראל arrived in נִיסָן, any grain in the fields had been growing while the land belonged to the גוים. So it seems there was no grain that could be used.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the sixteenth of ניסן, before new grain may be eaten
The colleagues, the group of scholars in the בית מדרש
'Your harvest,' teaching that the עומר must come from Jewish-owned grain
'The Merciful One,' a name for ה׳ when quoting the Torah

steps.whyThisMatters: The answer to this question, which comes later, will show that the חכמים do judge exactly when grain has reached a third. That is why רבי ירמיה took back his question.

phrases.english: For the colleagues asked רב כהנא:
The עומר that בני ישראל brought
when they entered the land,
from where did they bring it?
If you say it was from grain that grew in the hands of a גוי,
the Torah says 'your harvest' —
and not the harvest of a גוי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the case that explains why רבי ירמיה retracted in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What grain the first עומר in ארץ ישראל came from, given that grain grown by a גוי is not allowed.

steps.title: Maybe they never brought a עומר at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the question itself: how do we know they brought a עומר that year at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know they brought one? Maybe they did not bring one!
steps.whatsHappening: Before answering, the גמרא questions what the scholars assumed. Maybe there is no puzzle, because no עומר was brought that first year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question 'from where?' only makes sense if a עומר was actually brought. If they skipped it, the whole problem disappears.

phrases.english: How do we know that they brought it?
Maybe they did not bring it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the basic assumption behind the question in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that a עומר was brought when בני ישראל entered the land
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If no עומר was brought, there is nothing to ask about where it came from.

steps.title: The פסוק proves they brought the עומר
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק in יהושע says they ate the new grain 'on the day after פסח,' which shows they waited until after bringing the עומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't think that, because it is written: 'And they ate from the grain of the land on the day after פסח.' On the day after פסח they ate, but before that they did not. This means they brought the עומר first and then ate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea that no עומר was brought. It brings a פסוק showing that they waited to eat the new grain until the sixteenth of ניסן, the day the עומר is brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: New grain may not be eaten until the עומר is brought on the sixteenth of ניסן. The פסוק stresses that they ate only from the day after פסח and not earlier. That means they first brought the עומר, so the question in step 9 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't think that, a rejection of a suggestion
On the day after פסח, the sixteenth of ניסן

phrases.english: Don't think that, for it is written:
'And they ate from the grain of the land
on the day after פסח.'
On the day after פסח, they ate;
before that, they did not eat.
That is because they brought the עומר and only then ate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 with a פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe no עומר was brought in the first year.
steps.terutzMaskana: The timing of their eating shows they brought the עומר first.

steps.title: So where did they bring it from?
steps.stepSummary: Now that we know they brought a עומר, the גמרא repeats the original question: from where?
steps.simpleTranslation: So from where did they bring it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the scholars' question from step 9, which now stands even stronger. This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the פסוק proves a עומר was brought, the problem of 'your harvest' and not the harvest of a גוי comes right back. Some kind of grain must have counted as Jewish harvest.

phrases.english: From where did they bring it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 11 confirms a עומר was brought, this repeats the question of step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which grain could count as 'your harvest' for the first עומר in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: רב כהנא explains where the עומר came from
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that any grain that had not reached one-third of its growth while owned by a גוי counts as Jewish grain, and could be used for the עומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Any grain that did not reach one-third of its growth while in the hands of a גוי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers the question from Step 12. He says the עומר came from grain that had not yet reached one-third of its growth before בני ישראל took over the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that grain is considered 'grown' at one-third of its growth. If it reached that point after a Jew owned it, it counts as 'your harvest,' even though a גוי planted it. So there was grain they could use for the עומר.

keyTerms.meaning: One-third, meaning one-third of the grain's full growth
In the hands (ownership) of a non-Jew
Literally 'brought'; here it means 'reached' a stage of growth

steps.whyThisMatters: This one-third rule is the key to the whole discussion. Next, רבי ירמיה uses it to prove that חכמים can tell whether grain reached one-third.

phrases.english: He said to them:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רב כהנא, answering the scholars from Step 9.

phrases.english: Any grain that did not reach one-third of its growth
in the hands of a non-Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the repeated question from Step 12 about where the עומר came from.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Grain that had not reached one-third of its growth while a גוי owned it counts as Jewish grain.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה proves the חכמים can tell when grain reached one-third
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה argues that since they used this one-third rule for the עומר, they must have been able to tell whether grain reached one-third. So the חכמים can tell this in other cases too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the grain had reached one-third and they could not tell? Rather, they could tell. Here too, they can tell.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה uses רב כהנא's answer as proof. If בני ישראל relied on the one-third rule, they must have been able to tell whether grain had reached one-third.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a possible worry: maybe the grain passed one-third and nobody could know for sure. But they did bring the עומר, so they must have been able to tell. That shows the חכמים can make this judgment, which is why רבי ירמיה said his question was not a real question (Step 8).

keyTerms.meaning: But maybe; introduces a possibility that weakens an argument
Literally 'entered'; here it means the grain reached the one-third stage
They know for certain; they can tell
Here too; applying the same idea to our case

phrases.english: But maybe the grain had reached one-third
phrases.notes: Literally 'maybe it entered,' meaning it entered the stage of one-third growth while the גוי owned it.

phrases.english: and they could not tell for certain?
Rather, they could tell for certain.
Here too, they can tell for certain.
phrases.notes: 'Here' is רבי ירמיה's original case, telling whether grain reached one-third before ראש השנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב כהנא's answer as proof for רבי ירמיה's point.
steps.raayaObject: The חכמים can tell for certain whether grain reached one-third of its growth.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that בני ישראל brought the עומר using the one-third rule when they entered the land.

steps.title: Maybe the grain had not grown at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof: maybe the grain there had not grown at all, which is easy to see. But if grain grew about a quarter, maybe nobody can tell if it is a little under or over one-third.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the grain had not grown at all. But where it grew one-quarter, they cannot tell the difference between one-third and less than one-third!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי ירמיה's proof. It suggests the grain in יהושע's time was so young that it was obviously under one-third.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the grain had not grown at all, nobody needed fine judgment, because anyone could see it. That case would not prove we can tell the difference in a hard, close case, like grain at one-quarter. So the proof may not work.

phrases.english: But maybe the grain had not grown at all,
but where it reached one-quarter of its growth,
between one-third and less than one-third
they cannot tell for certain!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה's proof that the חכמים can tell whether grain reached one-third.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The proof only works if the grain was close to one-third. If it had not grown at all, that is an easy case and proves nothing about close cases.

steps.title: Grain could not ripen in five days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge using a פסוק: בני ישראל crossed the ירדן on the tenth of the month. Grain that had not grown at all could not be ready for the עומר just five days later.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not think so, because it is written: 'And the people came up from the ירדן on the tenth of the month.' If you think the grain had not grown at all, could it fully ripen in five days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 15. It shows from a פסוק in יהושע that the grain must have already grown some when בני ישראל arrived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They arrived on the tenth of ניסן, and the עומר is brought right after פסח, only about five days later. Grain cannot grow from nothing to ripe in five days, so it had already grown somewhat. That means they had to judge carefully whether it passed one-third, so רבי ירמיה's proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not think so; that idea is wrong
As it is written (introducing a פסוק)
On the tenth of the month

steps.whatToRemember: For now the proof seems to hold: grain that was already partly grown would have to be judged at the one-third point. Steps 17–18 knock this answer down, so this is not the final word.

phrases.english: Do not think so,
as it is written: 'And the people came up from the Jordan
on the tenth of the month,'
and if you think
that the grain had not grown at all,
could it fully ripen in five days?
phrases.notes: Five days counts from the tenth of the month until the עומר was brought, right after פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 15 and keeps the proof from Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a פסוק that rules out the challenge's scenario
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The grain may have had no growth at all, which would be easy to judge.
steps.terutzMaskana: The grain must have already grown some, since it could not ripen in five days, so they had to judge the one-third point and could do so.

steps.title: Even a quarter-grown crop could not ripen in five days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on step 16. Grain that had grown a quarter or a sixth also could not be fully ripe in only five days.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what will you say instead, that the grain had grown a quarter or a sixth? Even then, could it be fully grown in five days?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the answer from step 16. That answer said grain with no growth could not be ready in five days. The גמרא points out that grain with only a little growth has the same problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 tried to prove the grain must have been partly grown. But a quarter-grown crop also cannot ripen in five days by nature. So the five-day argument does not show that the grain was partly grown.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מַאי, דְּעָיֵיל רִבְעָא אוֹ דַנְקָא?
phrases.english: Rather, what? That it had grown a quarter or a sixth?
Still, in five days
could it become fully grown?!
phrases.notes: Five days means from crossing the ירדן on the tenth until the עומר on the sixteenth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי, דְּעָיֵיל רִבְעָא אוֹ דַנְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reply given in step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The step 16 claim that the grain must have been partly grown, since no-growth grain could not ripen in five days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Partly grown grain also cannot ripen in five days, so the five-day argument proves nothing

steps.title: 'Land of the deer' explains it, so the proof falls
steps.stepSummary: The only answer is that ארץ ישראל is called 'ארץ צבי', where grain ripens very fast. That works just as well for grain that had not grown at all, so רבי ירמיה's proof falls.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what must you say? It is called 'the land of the deer' (its grain ripens fast). Then here too, with no growth at all, 'the land of the deer' is said about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the only answer left: grain in ארץ ישראל ripens quickly. That same answer lets the grain start from zero, so the challenge in step 15 stands again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If fast ripening explains a quarter-grown crop, it can also explain a crop with no growth. So we cannot prove the חכמים judged a crop near one-third. רבי ירמיה's proof from the עומר is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The land of the deer', a name for ארץ ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: The עומר proof does not show the חכמים can tell whether grain reached a third. The grain may have had no growth at all and ripened fast in 'ארץ צבי'.

phrases.english: Rather, what do you have to say?
'The land of the deer' is written about it
phrases.notes: דניאל 11:41. Its grain ripens as fast as a deer runs.

phrases.english: Here too:
'the land of the deer' is written about it.
phrases.notes: So even grain with zero growth could ripen in time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the result of step 17's problem
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי ירמיה's proof (step 14) that the חכמים can tell when grain reached one-third
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Fast ripening in 'ארץ צבי' explains the case even with no growth, so the case says nothing about judging one-third

steps.title: רבי חנינא: 'אסיף' does not mean harvest
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא attacks the earlier proof that read 'אסיף' as harvesting. Another פסוק uses 'gathering' for collecting the leftover waste of the threshing floor and winepress.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא challenged it: Can you really say this 'אסיף' means harvest? But it is written 'when you gather from your threshing floor and from your winepress', and the Master said that פסוק speaks about the waste of the threshing floor and winepress!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to an earlier proof that came from the word 'אסיף', which it had read as harvest. רבי חנינא says the word does not have to mean harvest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proof needed 'אסיף' at סוכות to mean cutting the grain. רבי חנינא shows that 'gathering' at סוכות means collecting leftover straw and waste. If so, the word tells us nothing about the grain harvest.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftover waste of the threshing floor and winepress

phrases.english: רבי חנינא challenged it:
And can you really say
that this 'gathering' means harvest?
phrases.notes: This is the word from 'חג האסיף' that was used earlier as a source.

phrases.english: But it is written: 'When you gather from your threshing floor and from your winepress',
and the Master said:
the verse speaks of the waste of the threshing floor and winepress!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the עומר discussion and attacks the proof from 'אסיף' in steps 3–4
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier reading of 'אסיף' as harvesting
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A parallel פסוק about סוכות uses 'gathering' for collecting waste, not for harvesting

steps.title: רבי זירא: the proof has been chopped down
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא admits that the proof they relied on has been destroyed by רבי חנינא's challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: We had this matter firmly in our hands, and רבי חנינא came and swung an axe into it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא accepts רבי חנינא's challenge. He says the old proof no longer works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer is given to רבי חנינא. רבי זירא's picture of an axe shows the proof is fully cut down. That leaves the one-third rule without a source.

phrases.english: רבי זירא said:
This matter was in our hands,
phrases.notes: He means: we thought we had a solid proof.

phrases.english: and רבי חנינא came
and threw an axe into it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts step 19's challenge
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The proof from 'אסיף' is rejected, and a new source is needed

steps.title: So where do we learn it from?
steps.stepSummary: With the old proof gone, the גמרא asks again for a source for the one-third rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא asks for a new source and is preparing to bring a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule itself is not dropped; only its proof failed. So the גמרא looks for a different source that grain's year depends on reaching one-third.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it?

phrases.english: Rather, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the collapse of the proof in step 20
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A new source for the rule that grain's year depends on reaching one-third of its growth

steps.title: A ברייתא of רבי יונתן בן יוסף begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא in which רבי יונתן בן יוסף quotes the פסוק about grain lasting three years.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יונתן בן יוסף says: 'And it shall produce the grain for the three years'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its new source by quoting a ברייתא. The quote is not finished yet; the explanation comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far, only the פסוק is quoted. רבי יונתן בן יוסף will learn the one-third idea from the word 'שלש' (three) in the פסוק. That explanation continues past this point.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not finished here. Do not try to work out the proof yet; it comes in the next lines.

phrases.aramaic: כִּדְתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן יוֹסֵף אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it was taught: רבי יונתן בן יוסף says:
'And it shall produce the grain
for the three years',

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן יוֹסֵף אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא of רבי יונתן בן יוסף based on 'לשלש השנים' (ויקרא 25:21), still in progress
